facts.text: Model fidelity is the amount of physical detail included in a model; braking fidelity ranges from a lookup table or single formula through a point-mass model with measured delays to full multibody simulation with soil.
facts.quote: Model fidelity is how much physical detail a model includes; for braking, the levels run from a lookup table or single formula, through a point-mass model with measured delays, to a full multibody simulation with soil.

facts.text: Increasing braking-model detail costs more time and data and introduces more chances to be wrong; extra detail pays off only when it changes the answer.
facts.quote: more detail costs more time, more data and more chances to be wrong, and it pays off only when the extra detail changes the answer.

facts.text: The simplest stopping-distance model is the constant-deceleration equation d = v^2 / (2a), augmented with grade and mass terms, and requires hours of effort.
facts.quote: Constant-deceleration equation, `d = v^2 / (2a)` plus grade and mass terms. Hours of effort.

facts.text: The constant-deceleration stopping-distance equation is the basis of ISO 3450, the US mining rule and the New South Wales formulas.
facts.quote: The basis of ISO 3450, the US mining rule and the New South Wales formulas.

facts.text: A constant-deceleration stopping-distance model is useful for sanity checks and conservative envelopes but misses delay, brake build-up, variable traction and stability.
facts.quote: Good for sanity checks and conservative envelopes; misses delay, build-up, variable traction and stability.

facts.text: A point-mass transient braking model includes measured latency, a brake build-up lag and deceleration maps giving available deceleration by grade, payload, surface and drive state; the model requires low to moderate effort.
facts.quote: Point-mass transient model with measured latency, a brake build-up lag and deceleration maps (lookup tables of available deceleration by grade, payload, surface and drive state). Low to moderate effort.

facts.text: The booklet selects the point-mass transient braking model for the runtime trigger and large Monte Carlo sweeps.
facts.quote: The booklet's choice for the runtime trigger and for large Monte Carlo sweeps.

facts.text: Adding lumped brake hydraulics to a point-mass model represents pressure build-up and its spread and requires days to weeks of effort.
facts.quote: Point-mass plus lumped brake hydraulics: adds the pressure build-up and its spread. Days to weeks.

facts.text: A hydrostatic drivetrain braking model represents braking capacity as a function of operating state and requires weeks of effort.
facts.quote: Hydrostatic drivetrain model: braking capacity as a function of operating state. Weeks.

facts.text: A rigid multibody braking model with tire models and 3 to 8 degrees of freedom represents roll, yaw, jackknife and pitch under braking, is used to derive deceleration caps for turning and cross-slope, and requires weeks of effort.
facts.quote: Rigid multibody, 3 to 8 degrees of freedom, with tire models: roll, yaw, jackknife and pitch under braking; used to derive deceleration caps for turning and cross-slope. Weeks.

facts.text: Full multibody braking models with contact and detailed hydraulics or hydrostatics support design exploration and difficult transitions; these models are parameter-heavy and require months of effort.
facts.quote: Full multibody with contact and detailed hydraulics or hydrostatics: design exploration and difficult transitions. Months; parameter-heavy.

facts.text: Semi-empirical terramechanics using the Soil Contact Model represents soft-ground braking force and sinkage.
facts.quote: Semi-empirical terramechanics (Soil Contact Model): soft-ground braking force and sinkage.

facts.text: DEM, SPH or FEM terrain models are recommended only for selected braking limit cases.
facts.quote: DEM, SPH or FEM terrain: selected limit cases only.

facts.text: Reduced-order or surrogate braking models fitted to richer models enable millions of evaluations but are unsafe outside their training range.
facts.quote: Reduced-order or surrogate models fitted to the richer ones: millions of evaluations, but unsafe outside the range they were trained on.

facts.text: The booklet recommends selecting the lowest-fidelity braking model that predicts every safety-relevant output within a validated uncertainty envelope.
facts.quote: the right fidelity is "the lowest model that predicts every safety-relevant output within a validated uncertainty envelope" [Chapter 8]

facts.text: In a 2026 simulation round robin on a road braking case, point-mass implementations reproduced the prescribed deceleration exactly, while more complex vehicle models formed the extremes of a 0.033 s and 0.314 m spread; greater complexity did not imply greater accuracy.
facts.quote: in a 2026 simulation round robin on a road braking case, the point-mass implementations reproduced the prescribed deceleration exactly, while the more complex vehicle models formed the extremes of a 0.033 s and 0.314 m spread

facts.text: Higher braking-model fidelity pays off for brake-actuation hydraulics and latency spread, articulated and high-center-of-gravity stability during hard braking, hydrostatic drives with state-dependent capacity, and soft or deformable ground.
facts.quote: Higher fidelity pays off in four places: brake-actuation hydraulics (latency and its spread), articulated and high-center-of-gravity stability during hard braking, hydrostatic drives whose capacity varies with state, and soft or deformable ground [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The booklet recommends layered braking models per machine family rather than one ultimate digital twin: a fast threshold model for very large parameter sweeps, a stability challenge model to derive deceleration caps, and a high-fidelity model for selected edge cases that could invalidate simpler models.
facts.quote: a fast threshold model for very large parameter sweeps, a stability challenge model to derive deceleration caps, and a high-fidelity model for the selected edge cases that could invalidate the simpler ones

facts.text: The recommended layered braking simulation uses sensor simulation to supply detection delay and error to the braking simulation.
facts.quote: with sensor simulation feeding detection delay and error into the braking simulation [Chapter 8]

facts.text: No published source gives a universal off-road prediction error for any braking-model fidelity level.
facts.quote: No published source gives a universal off-road prediction error for any level

facts.text: Each braking-model fidelity level must be calibrated and checked against the program's own physical tests.
facts.quote: each must be calibrated and checked against the program's own physical tests [Chapter 8].
